lead.title: A bacterial nanosyringe retargeted to a plant receptor injects proteins, including a genome editor, into plant cells
lead.summary: A Caltech team re-engineered the Photorhabdus virulence cassette, an extracellular contractile injection system that this insect-pathogenic bacterium normally uses to fire proteins into insect cells, so that its tail fibres recognise the plant surface receptor FLS2 instead. The retargeted syringes delivered a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and an R2 retroelement genome editor into wild-type Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells, with Cre delivery efficiencies up to 16% in wild type and 75% of leaf cells in FLS2 overexpressing Arabidopsis. Delivery depended on FLS2 and scaled with how much receptor the cells carried, and the R2 cargo inserted a reporter gene into the genome that was then expressed. Getting proteins rather than DNA into intact plant cells is one of the hardest bottlenecks in plant biotechnology, so a receptor-programmable protein injector is a genuinely new route, though the work is so far confined to two model species and a reporter readout.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Signalling and metabolism news was mostly regulatory: osmotic stress drives rice OsbZIP13 into nuclear condensates that switch its binding from photosynthesis promoters to the ABA biosynthesis gene OsNCED3, local root phosphate sensing through PHR1 and PHL1 throttles the magnesium loader MGR4, and the kudzu allelochemical daidzin turns out to act by binding the WD40 domain of COP1 with a dissociation constant of 2.39 micromolar.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: Delivery and precision dominated alongside the lead: optimised tomato prime editors recreated a pepper resistance deletion in SlBs5 and SlBs5L and stacked it with SlDMR6 stop codons in one generation, a 14.54 Gb chromosome-scale genome landed for the Korean wheat cultivar Keumkang, and a methanol fixation nuclei protocol made single-nucleus sequencing work on soybean nodules, soybean seed and tomato fruit.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Prairie-relevant threads: a 250-line spring oat panel sown in autumn across five European sites gained 5 to 79% grain yield but took winterkill where frost sat between minus 5 and minus 8 degrees Celsius for more than four days, a machine-learning-designed five-strain root community raised alfalfa aboveground dry biomass 48.1% in saline-alkali field soil, and freeze-thaw aged microplastics proved more phytotoxic to rice roots than pristine ones, which matters for cold-region soils. None of today's items is a Canadian study.

plant.title: Osmotic stress pushes rice OsbZIP13 into condensates that switch it from growth to stress genes
plant.summary: Osmotic stress represses transcription of the rice transcription factor OsbZIP13 while stabilising the protein, which then undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation into nuclear condensates. RNA-seq, ChIP-seq and live-cell imaging show the condensates redirect its binding from photosynthetic gene promoters to the promoter of OsNCED3, turning on ABA biosynthesis and turning down photosynthesis. Overexpression lines were more drought and osmotic tolerant with higher photosynthetic rates, improved yield and delayed heading, while knockouts were hypersensitive. The yield claim rests on overexpression rather than a natural allele.

plant.title: Four independent mutations explain cannabigerol-dominant Cannabis sativa, and markers now track them
plant.summary: Disrupting the cannabinoid oxidocyclases that consume cannabigerolic acid leaves the precursor to accumulate, giving a cannabigerol-dominant chemotype. The authors mapped the haplotype architecture around four such mutations, including a structural variant that deletes cannabidiolic acid synthase outright, and compared them against homologous regions in more than 150 public assemblies to define 39 structurally distinct haplogroups at this highly variable locus. They built high-throughput markers for each mutated haplogroup and then generated more than 30 populations crossing the haplogroups against each other and against fully functional versions to test complementation.

plant.title: Root phosphate sensing sets how much magnesium the shoot gets
plant.summary: Phosphate scarcity is a far more common constraint than magnesium shortage, and this work shows plants ration the second according to the first. Local root phosphate status acts through the transcription factors PHR1 and PHL1, which directly repress MGR4, the main transporter loading magnesium into the xylem, so magnesium is not pushed into shoots whose growth is already arrested by low phosphate. As phosphate rises the repression lifts and magnesium moves again, sustaining shoot growth even when magnesium is limiting. The work is Arabidopsis-only and uses controlled nutrient media rather than soil.

plant.title: Daidzin, kudzu's allelochemical, inhibits root growth by binding COP1
plant.summary: The invasive vine Pueraria suppresses neighbouring vegetation partly through the isoflavonoid daidzin, and a chemical-genetic screen identifies the light signalling hub COP1 as the target. Daidzin inhibited root and hypocotyl elongation more strongly in the light, COP1 mutants resisted it and overexpressors were hypersensitive, and the compound promoted COP1 nuclear accumulation while depleting its substrate HY5. Thermal shift and microscale thermophoresis assays put direct binding at a dissociation constant of 2.39 micromolar, with docking pointing to the WD40 domain. Results are in Arabidopsis seedlings rather than in the field.

plant.title: Two salicylic acid glycosyltransferases block a virus without using hormones or RNA silencing
plant.summary: UGT74F1 and UGT74F2, long known as salicylic acid glycosyltransferases, turn out to be potent inhibitors of turnip mosaic virus. Overexpressing either one weakened local and systemic infection and losing UGT74F2 increased susceptibility, with UGT74F1 recruited to viral replication complexes. The resistance survived in sid2-4, coi1-23 and NahG backgrounds and in DCL2/4i and rdr6i plants, and a catalytically dead mutant that cannot make salicylic acid glucosides was still fully antiviral, which uncouples the enzyme activity from the immune one. The work is Arabidopsis-only.

plant.title: Vacuolar malate and fumarate transport matters for growth in C3 plants too
plant.summary: Malate and fumarate are a transient carbon store built during the day and emptied from the vacuole, a role well understood in C4 and CAM plants but unsettled in the C3 species that make up most land plants. Knocking out the vacuolar anion channels AtALMT4, AtALMT5 and AtALMT9 together to block transport into the vacuole caused a dramatic growth defect. Metabolic and fluxomic analysis traced the damage to carbon and nitrogen metabolism along with cellular pH and ionic homeostasis. An Arabidopsis-only, multiple-knockout result.

plant.title: APRR2 sets squash rind colour by switching on a magnesium chelatase subunit
plant.summary: APRR2 transcription factors have been tied to chlorophyll levels in fruits and rinds across many crops without a clear mechanism. In squash, Cucurbita pepo, a Cornell group shows CpAPRR2-A directly activates CpCHLH, the magnesium chelatase H subunit gene, by binding RGATTY elements in its promoter. Functional alleles gave dark green rinds with high chlorophyll and high CpCHLH expression, a mutated version gave pale rinds, and silencing dropped both. The same relationship held in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, suggesting the link is conserved.

plant.title: How hard the drought was decides whether wheat grain weight recovers after rain
plant.summary: Two years of field experiments with carbon-13 labelling, transcriptomics and enzymology show that recovery after drought is not simply the stress running backwards. Moderate drought followed by rewatering shifted stem metabolism from fructan hydrolysis toward starch biosynthesis and raised 1000-grain weight, with labelling confirming assimilates went preferentially to the spikes. Severe drought kept 1-fructan exohydrolase active and starch synthesis genes suppressed, cutting 1000-grain weight. Exogenous spermidine restored much of the loss, and the drought-tolerant genotype XN836 outperformed the sensitive XN979 in both carbon transport and spermidine synthesis.

plant.title: The missing enzymes in iboga alkaloid biosynthesis are found, including an unexpected PR10 protein
plant.summary: Tabernanthe iboga makes voacangine, the semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine, but the pathway could never be reconstituted in a heterologous host. Combining bulk and single-cell gene expression from leaf and root, the authors identify the two enzymes that complete voacangine biosynthesis outside the plant, one of them a pathogenesis-related PR10 family protein that appears to cyclise a transient intermediate. The same expression data yielded four further enzymes converting a shared upstream intermediate into ibophyllidine, explaining how one precursor feeds two structurally distinct alkaloid classes.

plant.title: A MYB and ABF pair routes melatonin synthesis into citrus rootstock drought tolerance
plant.summary: In trifoliate orange, Poncirus trifoliata, the chloroplast-localised melatonin biosynthesis gene PtrASMT1 is induced by drought, ABA and melatonin itself. Overexpression raised melatonin and eased oxidative damage while virus-induced silencing increased drought sensitivity, and pharmacological blocks confirmed the effect runs through melatonin. PtrMYB82, induced by dehydration and melatonin but not ABA, binds and activates the PtrASMT1 promoter, while the ABA-responsive PtrABF2 also promotes it and is itself regulated by PtrMYB82; the two proteins interact to boost transcription together. Greenhouse and transgenic or silenced material, not field trials.

biotech.title: A retargeted bacterial injection system delivers proteins and a genome editor into plant cells
biotech.summary: The Photorhabdus virulence cassette is a phage-tail-like nanomachine that injects proteins into insect cells, and engineering its tail fibres to recognise the plant receptor FLS2 made it work on plants. A library of FLS2-targeting cassettes delivered a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and an R2 retroelement genome editor, reaching up to 16% efficiency in wild-type Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells and 75% of leaf cells in FLS2 overexpressors. R2 delivery inserted and expressed a reporter gene. Model species and reporter cargo only, so crop delivery remains to be shown.

biotech.title: Optimised prime editors recreate a pepper resistance allele in tomato and stack it with a second one
biotech.summary: Three tomato prime editors, TomPE2, TomPE6c and TomPE7, were used to delete two leucine residues from the CYSTM-domain proteins SlBs5 and SlBs5L, precisely recreating a resistance-associated deletion found naturally in pepper and giving tomato lines more resistant to Xanthomonas. Writing premature stop codons into the susceptibility gene SlDMR6 conferred resistance to both Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas syringae, and transcriptomes showed the two routes give different defence states, induced versus elevated basal. A modular multiplex system combined loci in a single generation, with edits inherited and resistance holding at elevated temperature. The research article published 30 October and was highlighted by the journal on 19 November.

biotech.title: A chromosome-scale genome for Keumkang, the first for a commercially grown Asian wheat variety
biotech.summary: Keumkang is a major winter wheat across the Korean Peninsula, valued for early heading, adaptation to a temperate monsoon climate and grain quality. Using PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore and Omni-C data, the team assembled 14.54 Gb with a contig N50 of 79.13 Mb and 98.81% BUSCO completeness. Annotation combining Iso-Seq, RNA-seq, protein homology, gene projection and ab initio prediction gave 255,293 gene models, 145,082 of them high confidence. It is a data resource rather than a trait result, and the first chromosome-scale assembly for a commercially cultivated Asian variety.

biotech.title: A methanol fixation protocol makes single-nucleus sequencing work on stubborn crop tissues
biotech.summary: Rigid cell walls and messy metabolomes have kept single-cell transcriptomics from spreading in plants. MF-PENS combines methanol fixation with percoll-enriched nuclei sorting, skipping fluorescence-activated nuclei sorting altogether and cutting RNA leakage. The authors validate it on fresh and frozen rice roots and leaves and on tissues usually considered recalcitrant, including soybean root nodules, soybean seeds and tomato fruits. Benchmarking reports better gene capture, clustering and cell type annotation accuracy than conventional protocols. It is a methods paper, so the gains are relative to the comparison protocols chosen.

biotech.title: Pre-screening guide RNAs for the many gene copies of mustard sets a multiplexing floor
biotech.summary: Polyploid Brassica juncea carries multiple homologs of most genes, so the authors pair in silico guide prediction with in vitro cleavage assays to pre-screen guides against MIR160 with 14 copies, MIR167 with 15, and the protein-coding CAMTA3. Cleavage assays showed both the number and the position of mismatches in the PAM-proximal seed region govern Cas9 activity, and several guides cut across multiple homologs. They recommend assembling at least eight and five guides respectively to edit all copies of MIR160 and MIR167, and validated the MIR160 guides in Arabidopsis as a heterologous system rather than in mustard itself.

biotech.title: Review: the moss Physcomitrium patens as a chassis for plant synthetic biology
biotech.summary: This review argues the spreading earthmoss beats Arabidopsis and maize for several synthetic biology jobs: shorter life cycle, easier handling, a haploid phase, and far higher efficiency of transgene integration by homologous recombination, plus the ability to maintain episomes as another route to expression. It surveys what has already been done in the system, including synthetic genomes, recombinant protein production, metabolic engineering and artificial organelle engineering, and the toolkits for transformation cassettes, DNA and RNA editing and reporters. The main limitation flagged is the high number of duplicated genes when native genes must be tuned.

biotech.title: Why enzymes make so few C-glycosides, worked out on a maize glycosyltransferase
biotech.summary: C-glycosides carry hydrolytically stable carbon to carbon bonds that make them valuable and hard to synthesise, and few enzymes are known to form them. Crystallography, biochemical assays and atomistic simulation of the maize C-glycosyltransferase ZmUGT708A6 reveal two flexible gates controlling substrate access and reactive conformations. Combined quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics simulations with mutational data support a stepwise electrophilic aromatic substitution mechanism for neutral phloretin, run by a catalytic histidine and aspartate dyad through a high-energy intermediate stabilised by a water-mediated proton transfer. Substrate hydroxylation patterns and protonation states then explain why the natural scope stays narrow.

biotech.title: Drying RNA on the extraction column lets virome surveillance skip the cold chain
biotech.summary: High-throughput sequencing is now central to plant virus surveillance, but field use stumbles on keeping RNA intact without refrigeration, a particular problem for chili pepper, Capsicum, whose tissues carry strong RNA-degrading activity. Retaining and dehydrating extracted RNA directly on the silica column kept it stable at ambient temperature, where conventionally extracted RNA degraded quickly. Validated on symptomatic Indonesian samples, RNA stayed highly intact through three days of ambient transport, and sequencing recovered near-complete genomes of Capsicum annuum amalgavirus 1, pepper cryptic virus 2 and chili veinal mottle virus plus begomovirus and polerovirus sequences, agreeing with PCR assays.

biotech.title: A three-tier screen mines marine microbes for immune inducers and growth promoters
biotech.summary: Two marine microbial libraries, 2,986 crude extracts and 2,747 purified compounds, were pushed through parallel three-tier cascades: a reactive oxygen species burst assay then whole-plant Arabidopsis resistance assays and rice field trials for immune inducers, and a DR5::GUS auxin reporter then seedling assays and rice yield traits for growth promoters. Metabolites L299, CR-222-8, HZA-5, 3J00027 and TWA-1 showed activity in the laboratory, with some carrying through to field effects on rice pest infestation or agronomic traits. The authors note field infestation by the striped stem borer Chilo suppressalis was unusually low, which weakens that comparison.

biotech.title: Overexpressing SlbHLH123 makes tomato more resistant to bacterial wilt
biotech.summary: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum is among the worst soil-borne threats to tomato. The transcription factor SlbHLH123 was rapidly and transiently induced on infection, and transgenic overexpression lines resisted wilt markedly better than wild type. Overexpressors accumulated less pathogen-induced reactive oxygen species and showed less membrane lipid peroxidation, with higher superoxide dismutase and peroxidase activity, and raised transcripts of the pathogenesis-related genes SlPR1b, SlPR4b and SlPR5. This is constitutive overexpression in a greenhouse assay rather than a natural allele or a field test.

ag.title: Autumn-sown spring oats gained 5 to 79% yield across five European sites, when the crop survived winter
ag.summary: Milder Central European winters have made autumn sowing of spring oat plausible, and a 250-line panel was sown both ways across five sites over two seasons. Winterkill hit four experiments, including total loss at one site-year, driven mainly by thin snow cover and frosts holding between minus 5 and minus 8 degrees Celsius for more than four days. Autumn sowing raised grain yield 5 to 79% through earlier development, less mildew and longer tillering, at the cost of more lodging. Canopy damage had a heritability of 0.55 and genomic prediction accuracy of 0.66, and GWAS on 14,614 SNPs found 17 robust associations clustering on 2D, which is novel, plus 4A and 4D near VRN1, 6D and 7D near VRN3.

ag.title: A machine-learning-designed five-strain community lifted alfalfa biomass 48.1% in saline-alkali field soil
ag.summary: Starting from 16S amplicon data and high-throughput cultivation, the group curated 327 salt-alkali-tolerant root-associated strains, then used genomics, functional profiling and pairwise interaction assays to pick 20 complementary strains and assembled 134 random communities tested in seed germination assays. Random forest and elastic-net models identified five key strains for the target community SP3. In pots under salt-alkali stress SP3 beat single and two-strain inoculations, raising alfalfa height 62.0% and root length 91.1%, and in saline-alkali field soil it raised aboveground dry biomass 48.1% over untreated controls. One field site and one crop so far.

ag.title: A wheat crown rot fungus secretes a protease that both triggers immunity and drives virulence
ag.summary: Fusarium pseudograminearum, cause of Fusarium crown rot, secretes many proteins whose roles are unclear. The subtilisin-like protease FpSBT1 induced cell death in Nicotiana benthamiana, requiring its I9 and S8 domains and the catalytic residues Asp169, His200 and Ser356, and acting independently of the immune co-receptors BAK1 and SOBIR1 while triggering multiple immune responses. Deleting FpSBT1 cut pathogenicity, conidiation and hyphal penetration, whereas deleting the homolog FpSBT2 alone did nothing, though the double mutant had extra growth defects. Neither protease was involved in abiotic stress tolerance.

ag.title: A Trichoderma strain halved brown rot severity in unwounded plums
ag.summary: Of six Trichoderma isolates with antagonistic activity against six plum pathogens, Trichoderma wujiangense T40 inhibited Monilinia fructicola most strongly at 86%. T40 restricted lesions in wounded fruit and cut the disease severity index by about 50% in unwounded fruit, and treated healthy fruit was firmer though lower in soluble solids, titratable acidity and sugars. Genome analysis predicted a broader biosynthetic gene cluster repertoire in T40 than in the pathogen, and confrontation assays showed T40 shifting toward secondary metabolism and degradation while the pathogen raised efflux and stress responses and lowered virulence and central metabolism. Postharvest fruit assays, not orchard trials.

ag.title: Nanocarrier fungicides cut what sprayers inhale but accumulated more in mouse tissue
ag.summary: Triazole fungicides formulated with titanium dioxide, silicon carbide or tea saponin carriers were compared against their conventional active ingredients. The nanocarrier formulations reduced inhalation unit exposure to prothioconazole and triadimefon by 50 to 90% during spraying, yet after 28 days of inhalation exposure in C57BL/6J female mice they accumulated more in tissue, especially liver and kidney, in a way linked to particle size. The carriers worsened pesticide-induced lung inflammation through oxidative stress and disturbed gut microbial composition, and carriers alone showed endocrine-disrupting signals including a lower estradiol to testosterone ratio and higher luteinising hormone. A rodent exposure study, not human monitoring.

ag.title: A qPCR seedling assay predicts field efficacy of barley loose smut seed treatments
ag.summary: Ustilago nuda, which causes loose smut of barley, stays asymptomatic until flowering, so evaluating seed treatments normally means growing plants out and inspecting them. An Agroscope group grew seedlings for 5, 10 and 14 days either on filter paper in the dark or in potting soil under light-dark cycles, from two naturally infected seed lots left untreated or treated with a synthetic fungicide or warm water, and quantified pathogen DNA relative to host DNA. Ten days on filter paper and 14 days in potting soil tracked two seasons of field disease incidence most closely and separated treatments clearly.

ag.title: Tomato yellow ring orthotospovirus turns up in Israel across vegetables, ornamentals and weeds
ag.summary: Tomatoes in the Hefer valley showed leaf yellowing with black ring spots in February 2024 that looked like tomato spotted wilt but tested negative for it, and similar symptoms appeared in neighbouring Capsicum annuum along with mosaic and deformed flowers in Cyclamen persicum and necrosis in Impatiens hawkeri. Sequencing recovered the tripartite genome of tomato yellow ring orthotospovirus, previously unrecorded in the country, confirmed by RT-PCR, ELISA and western blot. A host range study found fifteen susceptible species including the weeds Amaranthus viridis and Datura stramonium, which could act as reservoirs, and disease spread between plants at four growers through 2024.

ag.title: A native sunflower rhizobacterium raised survival under root rot pressure to 93.33%
ag.summary: Rhizoctonia solani root rot constrains sunflower production worldwide. Of 75 bacterial isolates from healthy sunflower rhizospheres, 21 were antagonistic in vitro, and in the greenhouse the isolates differed widely in both pathogen suppression and growth promotion. The best biocontrol isolate, B7, assigned provisionally to the Bacillus cereus group by 16S sequencing, raised sunflower survival under pathogen pressure to 93.33%, while isolates closest to Pseudomonas chlororaphis and Bacillus toyonensis did more for growth traits. Expression analysis linked B7 to changes across six defence transcripts spanning antifungal, salicylic acid, oxidative stress and phenylpropanoid markers. Greenhouse only.

ag.title: Freeze-thaw aged microplastics hurt rice roots more than fresh ones
ag.summary: Freeze-thaw cycling ages microplastics faster in cold-region soils, and this study compared pristine and aged polystyrene, PVC and polyethylene on rice roots. Aging oxidised and fragmented surfaces, raising hydrodynamic diameters 8.8 to 26.7% and negative surface charge by 5.17 to 5.36 millivolts. Aged PVC was the most phytotoxic, breaking root membrane integrity and suppressing superoxide dismutase activity by up to 54%, with malate depleted and lactate accumulating. Bisulfite sequencing found methylation changes dominated by the CHH context at over 96% of differentially methylated regions, including hypermethylation at redox hubs such as NTRC and Trx M3. A controlled exposure study rather than field soil.

ag.title: Agricultural commodity markets are harder to weaponise than the worry suggests
ag.summary: Part of a Nature Food collection on the geopolitics of food, this piece pushes back on fears that countries will use dominant export or import shares to choke off key commodities. The authors argue agricultural markets resist weaponisation beyond the time needed to find new suppliers or destinations: countries that lean heavily on one supplier usually have alternatives during disruptions, export markets for most commodities have grown less concentrated as regional suppliers emerged, and exporters generally have many markets to turn to if one closes. It is an analysis and comment piece rather than new empirical work, and the same issue carries pieces arguing the structural vulnerabilities are real.

methods: Coverage window: 19 to 21 November 2026 (about 48 hours). The previous issue was 2026-11-20, so no widening was needed and nothing was skipped. Items were found through PubMed searches filtered on entry date across plant science, biotechnology, genomics, pathology, entomology and pest management journals, and every date in this issue comes from the PubMed record. Publisher and news sites were again unreachable from this session: direct fetches to www.nature.com and to the NCBI E-utilities endpoint were both refused by the session's egress proxy, so dates could not be checked against publisher pages and those hosts would need to be allowed in the session's network settings. Two news threads surfaced by web search are therefore mentioned here rather than listed as items, because neither date nor detail could be confirmed against a primary source: a BASF statement reported on 16 November 2026 that its Nemasphere nematode-resistance trait for soybean is on track for commercial availability in the United States and Brazil, which is a company claim, and a Penn State CRISPR-edited cacao line reported on 1 November 2026 as entering field trials for black pod resistance. Earlier November reports of UK Defra clearance for two Phytoform gene-edited tomato traits and of a Bayer licence for University of California, Davis nitrogen-fixation editing technology also remain unconfirmed and were carried over unlisted from previous issues. Today's briefing is journal-only as a result. Arabidopsis-only results are flagged: the phosphate and magnesium allocation work, the daidzin and COP1 study, the UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 antiviral lines and the vacuolar ALMT knockouts; the lead's protein delivery results are also confined to Arabidopsis and Nicotiana benthamiana with reporter cargo. Also flagged are constitutive overexpression rather than natural alleles (OsbZIP13, SlbHLH123, PtrASMT1), greenhouse, pot and postharvest results without field data (the sunflower rhizobacteria, the Trichoderma plum trials, the microplastic exposures), a rodent inhalation study standing in for operator exposure, guides validated in a heterologous species rather than in Brassica juncea itself, and two reviews plus one comment piece. The tomato prime editing item is dated to the 19 November journal highlight; the underlying research article published on 30 October, which is stated in its summary. The citrus melatonin and Poncirus paper carries only a month in PubMed and is dated to its 20 November entry. No preprints are included, and no company claim is listed as an item. Items from the 17 and 20 November issues were not repeated, including the OsWIH2 planthopper peptide, the pear metabolome, the Ryd4 barley hybrid, the DNNGP-Pro prediction platform, the sugarcane mosaic virus vector, the tetraploid potato knockout guide, EPFL9 poplar editing, the cool-night blast work, the phytochrome A and COP1 study, the sugarcane borer genomic selection and the crabgrass and sunflower looper resistance surveys.
